clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon's stroke in June 1991, within a few months: your wrist injury stopped your playing and your anxiety rose; you and Rafe clashed and he moved out; you got high alone in your room; by early 1992 you were lost and low, unable to get going, with your grandfather gone and your mother about to remarry, and your grandmother Winifred was treated for thyroid cancer within a year of his death. Your father's shift toward his own father Clifford in early 1989, after years away, sat at the opening, and your mother's wedding to Desmond in autumn 1992 closed the period. Your move to Quarry Lane in spring 1989 and the settling at Hollin Road in the autumn, alongside your dropping chess and debate, mark the years before the injury. You found your drive again by early 1994 with an exchange in Lisbon and Porto; by then you were stung that your dad had never heard of the film you were making, reaching toward him. The shifts pile up most thickly from the autumn of 1991 through the winter and spring of 1992.
clusters.change: The opening sits with your grandfather Clifford's return in early 1989, before the injury in late 1991; the period now reaches from his return to your mother's wedding to Desmond in autumn 1992, with the injury and its aftermath as the centre of your trouble.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Winifred's diagnosis of bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002, within months: your anxiety rose and your functioning fell as you ran out of steam for performing; you had a disastrous audition for the national orchestra in early 2002 and were done with performing; by autumn 2002 you were on poor terms with family and friends, at distance from your parents; you left Thornbury for Gull Harbour. You met Marisol at a winter party in 2003 and left Gull Harbour to live with her, but split within the year and sank into a deep depression. You could not face your family; your parents seemed a world away. You relied on friends, and your dad spoke with Corbin who took you in. Her final months were spent in your parents' home in autumn 2003. She died in February 2004. The period settled as you began swimming, requested help with therapy costs, and returned to your therapist; your functioning came back up. Every shift in these months is yours and your parents', with your grandmother's illness and death at the centre.
clusters.change: The period now reaches from the autumn of 2002, when you moved away and grew distant from family, through to early 2004 when you returned to therapy and your functioning rose; the diagnosis sits in 2001 or 2002, and the disastrous audition and your distance from family in autumn 2002 mark where the period tightens.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within months: you were too drained for conversation with your mother; she pressed to visit you at Alder Creek and you kept the door shut on her; you left for nursing school in Marlow Sound in August 2008 and stopped speaking to her, a cutoff that held for roughly a year. Your aunt Imogen had a stroke in early 2009 with months of rehabilitation, widening the family's trouble. Your functioning rises once you are in nursing school, suggesting the cutoff from your mother steadied you, though the silence cost. The period is held by the months around your grandmother's death and the lodge visit, when contact with your mother became too much.
